functions.name: ASCII
functions.doc: Returns the ASCII code of the leftmost character in a character expression.

functions.name: CHAR
functions.doc: Converts an integer code (0-255) into its single-byte character; values outside that range return NULL.

functions.name: CHARINDEX
functions.doc: Returns the 1-based position of the first occurrence of one string within another, or 0 when absent. start_location sets where searching begins; bigint is returned for max types.

functions.name: CONCAT
functions.doc: Joins two or more values into a single string. NULL arguments become empty strings and non-string values are implicitly converted.

functions.name: CONCAT_WS
functions.doc: Joins values into one string with the separator between each pair. NULL values, and their separators, are skipped.

functions.name: DIFFERENCE
functions.doc: Compares the SOUNDEX codes of two strings and returns 0 to 4; 4 indicates the closest phonetic match.

functions.name: FORMAT
functions.doc: Formats a numeric or date/time value with a .NET format string and optional culture (e.g. 'en-US'). Returns NULL for an invalid format; relies on the CLR so it is comparatively slow.

functions.name: LEFT
functions.doc: Returns the given number of characters from the start of a string.

functions.name: LEN
functions.doc: Returns the character count of a string, not counting trailing spaces. Returns bigint for varchar(max), nvarchar(max) or varbinary(max) input.

functions.name: LOWER
functions.doc: Returns the string with all uppercase characters converted to lowercase.

functions.name: LTRIM

signatures.doc: SQL Server 2022+: strips any of the listed characters instead of spaces.

functions.doc: Removes leading spaces from a string. From SQL Server 2022 an optional second argument specifies the characters to remove.

functions.name: NCHAR
functions.doc: Returns the Unicode character for the given integer code point.

functions.name: PATINDEX
functions.doc: Returns the 1-based start position of the first match of a LIKE-style pattern (wildcards allowed, usually wrapped in %) in an expression, or 0 if there is no match.

functions.name: QUOTENAME
functions.doc: Wraps a string in delimiters (square brackets by default) to make a valid delimited identifier, doubling embedded closing delimiters. Input over 128 characters returns NULL.

functions.name: REPLACE
functions.doc: Replaces every occurrence of string_pattern in a string with string_replacement. Matching follows the input collation.

functions.name: REPLICATE
functions.doc: Repeats a string the given number of times; a negative count returns NULL. Output is capped at 8000 bytes unless the input is a max type.

functions.name: REVERSE
functions.doc: Returns the characters of a string in reverse order.

functions.name: RIGHT
functions.doc: Returns the given number of characters from the end of a string.

functions.name: RTRIM

signatures.doc: SQL Server 2022+: strips any of the listed characters instead of spaces.

functions.doc: Removes trailing spaces from a string. From SQL Server 2022 an optional second argument specifies the characters to remove.

functions.name: SOUNDEX
functions.doc: Returns a four-character code describing how a string sounds when spoken in English, for phonetic comparisons.

functions.name: SPACE
functions.doc: Returns a string made of the given number of spaces; a negative count returns NULL.

functions.name: STR
functions.doc: Converts a number to a right-justified string of total length (default 10) with the given decimal places (default 0). Returns asterisks if the value does not fit.

functions.name: STRING_ESCAPE
functions.doc: Escapes special and control characters in text using the rules of the given type. Only 'json' is currently supported.

functions.name: STUFF
functions.doc: Deletes length characters starting at the 1-based start position and inserts another string there. Returns NULL if start is out of range.

functions.name: SUBSTRING
functions.doc: Returns part of a character, binary, text or image value. start is 1-based; a start below 1 shortens the result instead of failing. A negative length raises an error.

functions.name: TRANSLATE
functions.doc: Replaces each character found in characters with the character at the same position in translations. Both lists must have equal length.

functions.name: TRIM

signatures.doc: Removes the listed characters instead of spaces.
SQL Server 2022+ (compatibility level 160): choose which side to trim.

functions.doc: Removes spaces, or a set of specified characters, from the start and end of a string.

functions.name: UNICODE
functions.doc: Returns the Unicode code point of the first character of the input.

functions.name: UPPER
functions.doc: Returns the string with all lowercase characters converted to uppercase.

functions.name: ABS
functions.doc: Returns the absolute (non-negative) value of a number, in the same type as the input.

functions.name: ACOS
functions.doc: Returns the angle in radians whose cosine is the given value, which must be between -1 and 1.

functions.name: ASIN
functions.doc: Returns the angle in radians whose sine is the given value, which must be between -1 and 1.

functions.name: ATAN
functions.doc: Returns the angle in radians whose tangent is the given value.

functions.name: ATN2
functions.doc: Returns the angle in radians between the positive x-axis and the ray to point (x, y), using both signs to pick the correct quadrant.

functions.name: CEILING
functions.doc: Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the value, keeping the input data type.

functions.name: COS
functions.doc: Returns the cosine of an angle given in radians.

functions.name: COT
functions.doc: Returns the cotangent of an angle given in radians.

functions.name: DEGREES
functions.doc: Converts an angle from radians to degrees, keeping the input data type.

functions.name: EXP
functions.doc: Returns e raised to the given power; the inverse of LOG.

functions.name: FLOOR
functions.doc: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to the value, keeping the input data type.

functions.name: LOG

signatures.doc: Logarithm in the given base (SQL Server 2012+).

functions.doc: Returns the natural logarithm of a positive number, or its logarithm in the specified base.

functions.name: LOG10
functions.doc: Returns the base-10 logarithm of a positive number.

functions.name: PI
functions.doc: Returns the constant pi as a float.

functions.name: POWER
functions.doc: Raises a number to the power y. The result type follows the first argument, so integer input gives an integer result.

functions.name: RADIANS
functions.doc: Converts an angle from degrees to radians, keeping the input data type (use a decimal input to avoid integer truncation).

functions.name: RAND
functions.doc: Returns a pseudo-random float from 0 up to, but not including, 1. A seed restarts the sequence. It is evaluated once per query reference, not once per row.

functions.name: ROUND

signatures.doc: A non-zero function value truncates instead of rounding.

functions.doc: Rounds a number to length decimal places; a negative length rounds to the left of the decimal point.

functions.name: SIGN
functions.doc: Returns -1, 0 or 1 for a negative, zero or positive input.

functions.name: SIN
functions.doc: Returns the sine of an angle given in radians.

functions.name: SQRT
functions.doc: Returns the square root of a non-negative number.

functions.name: SQUARE
functions.doc: Returns the value multiplied by itself.

functions.name: TAN
functions.doc: Returns the tangent of an angle given in radians.

functions.name: GREATEST
functions.doc: Returns the largest value among 1 to 254 comparable expressions, ignoring NULLs; returns NULL only if all are NULL.

functions.name: LEAST
functions.doc: Returns the smallest value among 1 to 254 comparable expressions, ignoring NULLs; returns NULL only if all are NULL.

functions.name: LEFT_SHIFT
functions.doc: Shifts the bits of an integer or binary value left by shift_amount positions; the result has the input type. Equivalent to the << operator.

functions.name: RIGHT_SHIFT
functions.doc: Shifts the bits of an integer or binary value right by shift_amount positions; the result has the input type. Equivalent to the >> operator.

functions.name: BIT_COUNT
functions.doc: Returns the number of bits set to 1 in an integer or binary value.

functions.name: GET_BIT
functions.doc: Returns the bit (0 or 1) at the given zero-based offset of an integer or binary value, counting from the least significant bit.

functions.name: SET_BIT
functions.doc: Returns the value with the bit at bit_offset set to bit_value (default 1). The result has the type of expression_value.

functions.name: GETDATE
functions.doc: Returns the current date and time of the database server as datetime, with no time zone offset.

functions.name: GETUTCDATE
functions.doc: Returns the current UTC date and time of the server as datetime.

functions.name: SYSDATETIME
functions.doc: Returns the current server date and time as datetime2(7), with more fractional precision than GETDATE.

functions.name: SYSUTCDATETIME
functions.doc: Returns the current UTC date and time of the server as datetime2(7).

functions.name: SYSDATETIMEOFFSET
functions.doc: Returns the current server date and time as datetimeoffset(7), including the server time zone offset.

functions.name: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
functions.doc: ANSI SQL equivalent of GETDATE(): the current server date and time as datetime. Written without parentheses.

functions.name: DATEADD
functions.doc: Adds a signed integer number of datepart units to a date and returns a value of the same type as the date argument.

functions.name: DATEDIFF
functions.doc: Returns the count of datepart boundaries crossed between startdate and enddate as int. Raises an overflow error if the result exceeds int; see DATEDIFF_BIG.

functions.name: DATEDIFF_BIG
functions.doc: Like DATEDIFF, but returns the count of datepart boundaries crossed as bigint, avoiding overflow for small units over long ranges.

functions.name: DATENAME
functions.doc: Returns a string for the given datepart of a date, e.g. the month or weekday name. Names depend on the session language.

functions.name: DATEPART
functions.doc: Returns an integer for the given datepart of a date. week and weekday results depend on SET DATEFIRST; iso_week uses ISO 8601 weeks.

functions.name: DAY
functions.doc: Returns the day of the month (1-31) of a date; same as DATEPART(day, date).

functions.name: MONTH
functions.doc: Returns the month number (1-12) of a date; same as DATEPART(month, date).

functions.name: YEAR
functions.doc: Returns the year of a date as an integer; same as DATEPART(year, date).

functions.name: EOMONTH
functions.doc: Returns the last day of the month containing start_date, optionally shifted by month_to_add months.

functions.name: DATEFROMPARTS
functions.doc: Builds a date from year, month and day integers. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL; invalid values raise an error.

functions.name: DATETIMEFROMPARTS
functions.doc: Builds a datetime value from its date and time parts. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL.

functions.name: DATETIME2FROMPARTS
functions.doc: Builds a datetime2 value from its parts; fractions is interpreted according to precision (a literal 0-7).

functions.name: DATETIMEOFFSETFROMPARTS
functions.doc: Builds a datetimeoffset value from date and time parts plus a time zone offset; fractions is interpreted using precision.

functions.name: SMALLDATETIMEFROMPARTS
functions.doc: Builds a smalldatetime value from year, month, day, hour and minute.

functions.name: TIMEFROMPARTS
functions.doc: Builds a time value from its parts; fractions is interpreted according to precision (a literal 0-7).

functions.name: SWITCHOFFSET
functions.doc: Returns the datetimeoffset value moved to another time zone offset (e.g. '-05:00'), keeping the same UTC instant.

functions.name: TODATETIMEOFFSET
functions.doc: Attaches a time zone offset to a date/time value, treating the input as local time in that offset; the clock time is not shifted.

functions.name: ISDATE
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the expression is a valid datetime or smalldatetime value, else 0. Depends on SET DATEFORMAT and LANGUAGE; does not accept datetime2-only ranges.

functions.name: DATE_BUCKET
functions.doc: Returns the start of the fixed-width bucket (number dateparts wide) that contains date, aligned to origin (default 1900-01-01). Result type matches date.

functions.name: DATETRUNC
functions.doc: Truncates a date or time value to the start of the given datepart, e.g. the first day of the month. Result type matches the input date type.

functions.name: CURRENT_TIMEZONE
functions.doc: Returns the name of the time zone used by the server or instance, e.g. (UTC+01:00) Amsterdam, Berlin.

functions.name: CURRENT_TIMEZONE_ID
functions.doc: Returns the Windows time zone ID of the server or instance, e.g. Pacific Standard Time, usable with AT TIME ZONE.

functions.name: AVG
functions.doc: Returns the average of non-NULL values in a group. Integer input produces an integer result. Can be used as a window aggregate with OVER.

functions.name: CHECKSUM_AGG
functions.doc: Returns a checksum of the values in a group, ignoring NULLs; useful for detecting changes in a table.

functions.name: COUNT
functions.doc: Returns the number of items in a group as int. COUNT(*) counts all rows; COUNT(expression) counts non-NULL values.

functions.name: COUNT_BIG
functions.doc: Like COUNT, but returns bigint. COUNT_BIG(*) counts all rows; COUNT_BIG(expression) counts non-NULL values.

functions.name: GROUPING
functions.doc: Returns 1 when the GROUP BY column is aggregated in the row (a ROLLUP, CUBE or GROUPING SETS subtotal), otherwise 0.

functions.name: GROUPING_ID
functions.doc: Returns an integer bitmap of GROUPING() results for the listed columns, identifying the grouping level of each row.

functions.name: MAX
functions.doc: Returns the highest non-NULL value in a group. Works with numeric, character, date and uniqueidentifier types.

functions.name: MIN
functions.doc: Returns the lowest non-NULL value in a group. Works with numeric, character, date and uniqueidentifier types.

functions.name: STDEV
functions.doc: Returns the sample statistical standard deviation of the values in a group.

functions.name: STDEVP
functions.doc: Returns the population statistical standard deviation of the values in a group.

functions.name: SUM
functions.doc: Returns the total of the non-NULL numeric values in a group. Can be used as a window aggregate with OVER.

functions.name: VAR
functions.doc: Returns the sample statistical variance of the values in a group.

functions.name: VARP
functions.doc: Returns the population statistical variance of the values in a group.

functions.name: STRING_AGG
functions.doc: Concatenates non-NULL values from a group into one string with a separator. Append WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) to control the order of values.

functions.name: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT
functions.doc: Returns an approximate count of distinct non-NULL values, using less memory than COUNT(DISTINCT) on large data sets (about 2% error).

functions.name: APPROX_PERCENTILE_CONT
functions.doc: Returns an approximate interpolated percentile (0.0-1.0) of a group. Use WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY expression). Suited to large data sets.

functions.name: APPROX_PERCENTILE_DISC
functions.doc: Returns an approximate percentile (0.0-1.0) value that exists in the group. Use WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY expression). Suited to large data sets.

functions.name: ROW_NUMBER
functions.doc: Assigns sequential numbers starting at 1 to rows within each partition. Requires OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).

functions.name: RANK
functions.doc: Returns the rank of each row within its partition; ties share a rank and leave gaps after them. Requires OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).

functions.name: DENSE_RANK
functions.doc: Returns the rank of each row within its partition; ties share a rank with no gaps. Requires OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).

functions.name: NTILE
functions.doc: Divides the ordered rows of each partition into the given number of groups and returns the group number. Requires OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).

functions.name: LAG
functions.doc: Returns a value from the row offset rows (default 1) before the current one, or default when none exists. Requires OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).

functions.name: LEAD
functions.doc: Returns a value from the row offset rows (default 1) after the current one, or default when none exists. Requires OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).

functions.name: FIRST_VALUE
functions.doc: Returns the first value in the ordered window frame. Use OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ... [ROWS|RANGE ...]); IGNORE NULLS allowed from 2022.

functions.name: LAST_VALUE
functions.doc: Returns the last value in the window frame. The default frame ends at the current row, so specify ROWS BETWEEN ... AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING for the partition end.

functions.name: CUME_DIST
functions.doc: Returns the cumulative distribution (0 < x <= 1) of a row within its partition. Requires OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).

functions.name: PERCENT_RANK
functions.doc: Returns the relative rank (0 to 1) of a row within its partition, (rank - 1) / (rows - 1). Requires OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).

functions.name: PERCENTILE_CONT
functions.doc: Returns an interpolated percentile (0.0-1.0) using WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY expr) OVER ([PARTITION BY ...]); the result may not exist in the data.

functions.name: PERCENTILE_DISC
functions.doc: Returns the smallest value whose cumulative distribution is >= percentile, using WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY expr) OVER ([PARTITION BY ...]).

functions.name: CAST
functions.doc: Converts an expression to the specified data type (ANSI syntax), e.g. CAST(x AS varchar(10)). Raises an error if the conversion fails.

functions.name: CONVERT
functions.doc: Converts an expression to the given data type; style controls date/time, money, float, binary and XML formatting (e.g. 112 = yyyymmdd).

functions.name: PARSE
functions.doc: Converts a string to a date/time or numeric type, optionally using a .NET culture. Raises an error on failure and requires the CLR.

functions.name: TRY_CAST
functions.doc: Like CAST, but returns NULL instead of an error when the conversion fails. Explicitly disallowed conversions still raise an error.

functions.name: TRY_CONVERT
functions.doc: Like CONVERT, but returns NULL instead of an error when the conversion fails. Explicitly disallowed conversions still raise an error.

functions.name: TRY_PARSE
functions.doc: Like PARSE, but returns NULL when the string cannot be converted. Requires the CLR.

functions.name: IIF
functions.doc: Returns true_value or false_value depending on a Boolean expression; shorthand for CASE WHEN. Can be nested up to 10 levels.

functions.name: CHOOSE
functions.doc: Returns the value at the given 1-based index from the list, or NULL if the index is out of range.

functions.name: COALESCE
functions.doc: Returns the first non-NULL argument. The result type follows data type precedence; it is shorthand for a CASE expression.

functions.name: NULLIF
functions.doc: Returns NULL when the two expressions are equal; otherwise returns the first expression.

functions.name: ISNULL
functions.doc: Returns replacement_value when check_expression is NULL, otherwise check_expression. The result has the type of check_expression.

functions.name: ISJSON

signatures.doc: Type constraint argument added in SQL Server 2022.

functions.doc: Returns 1 if the string is valid JSON, 0 if not, and NULL for NULL input. Optionally checks for a specific JSON type.

functions.name: JSON_VALUE
functions.doc: Extracts a scalar value from JSON at the given path. If the path is missing or not scalar, returns NULL in lax mode or errors in strict mode.

functions.name: JSON_QUERY
functions.doc: Extracts an object or array from JSON at the given path (whole input if omitted). A scalar at the path returns NULL in lax mode or errors in strict mode.

functions.name: JSON_MODIFY
functions.doc: Returns the JSON text with the value at path updated, inserted or appended (append prefix). In lax mode, a NULL new_value deletes the key.

functions.name: JSON_OBJECT
functions.doc: Builds a JSON object from zero or more key:value pairs. NULL ON NULL (default) keeps null values; ABSENT ON NULL omits them.

functions.name: JSON_ARRAY
functions.doc: Builds a JSON array from zero or more values. ABSENT ON NULL (default) skips NULLs; NULL ON NULL writes them as null.

functions.name: JSON_PATH_EXISTS
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the SQL/JSON path exists in the JSON input, 0 if it does not, and NULL for NULL input.

functions.name: OPENJSON

signatures.doc: Default schema: columns key, value, type.
Explicit schema maps properties to typed columns.

functions.doc: Table-valued function that parses JSON into rows of key/value/type, or typed columns via a WITH clause. Requires compatibility level 130 or higher.

functions.name: NEWID
functions.doc: Generates a new random unique value of type uniqueidentifier.

functions.name: NEWSEQUENTIALID
functions.doc: Generates a GUID greater than any previously generated by this function on the machine since Windows started. Only allowed in a DEFAULT constraint.

functions.name: SCOPE_IDENTITY
functions.doc: Returns the last identity value inserted in the current session and scope, unaffected by inserts made in triggers.

functions.name: IDENT_CURRENT
functions.doc: Returns the last identity value generated for the given table or view, in any session and any scope.

functions.name: IDENT_INCR
functions.doc: Returns the increment value defined for the identity column of a table or view.

functions.name: IDENT_SEED
functions.doc: Returns the original seed value defined for the identity column of a table or view.

functions.name: IDENTITY
functions.doc: Used only in SELECT ... INTO to add an identity column to the new table, e.g. IDENTITY(int, 1, 1) AS id.

functions.name: ERROR_LINE
functions.doc: Inside a CATCH block, returns the line number where the error occurred; NULL outside a CATCH block.

functions.name: ERROR_MESSAGE
functions.doc: Inside a CATCH block, returns the full text of the error message; NULL outside a CATCH block.

functions.name: ERROR_NUMBER
functions.doc: Inside a CATCH block, returns the error number that triggered it; NULL outside a CATCH block.

functions.name: ERROR_PROCEDURE
functions.doc: Inside a CATCH block, returns the name of the procedure or trigger where the error occurred, or NULL if none.

functions.name: ERROR_SEVERITY
functions.doc: Inside a CATCH block, returns the severity level of the error; NULL outside a CATCH block.

functions.name: ERROR_STATE
functions.doc: Inside a CATCH block, returns the state number of the error; NULL outside a CATCH block.

functions.name: XACT_STATE
functions.doc: Reports the transaction state of the session: 1 = active and committable, -1 = active but uncommittable (must roll back), 0 = no transaction.

functions.name: HOST_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the workstation name supplied by the client; it can be spoofed, so do not rely on it for security.

functions.name: HOST_ID
functions.doc: Returns the workstation identification number (client process ID) supplied by the client application.

functions.name: APP_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the application name set by the client for the current session; client-controlled, so not suitable for security checks.

functions.name: COMPRESS
functions.doc: Compresses a string or binary value using the GZIP algorithm and returns varbinary(max).

functions.name: DECOMPRESS
functions.doc: Decompresses a GZIP-compressed binary value; cast the result to the original string type to read it.

functions.name: FORMATMESSAGE

signatures.doc: Ad hoc printf-style message string (SQL Server 2016+).

functions.doc: Builds a message from sys.messages or a supplied format string, substituting %s/%d style placeholders with parameter values.

functions.name: ISNUMERIC
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the expression can convert to any numeric type, else 0. Accepts symbols like +, -, $ and ., so prefer TRY_CONVERT for validation.

functions.name: CHECKSUM
functions.doc: Computes an int hash over a row or a list of expressions, often used for hash indexes. Collisions are possible.

functions.name: BINARY_CHECKSUM
functions.doc: Computes a binary checksum over a row or expressions; unlike CHECKSUM it is sensitive to case and collation differences.

functions.name: HASHBYTES
functions.doc: Returns the hash of the input using the chosen algorithm. Only SHA2_256 and SHA2_512 are recommended; the input size limit was removed in 2016.

functions.name: ROWCOUNT_BIG
functions.doc: Returns the number of rows affected by the last statement as bigint; like @@ROWCOUNT for very large counts.

functions.name: SESSION_CONTEXT
functions.doc: Returns the value stored for a key in the session context (set with sp_set_session_context), or NULL if not set.

functions.name: CONTEXT_INFO
functions.doc: Returns the context_info value set for the current session or batch with SET CONTEXT_INFO.

functions.name: CURRENT_REQUEST_ID
functions.doc: Returns the ID of the current request within the current session.

functions.name: CURRENT_TRANSACTION_ID
functions.doc: Returns the transaction ID of the current transaction in the session.

functions.name: GET_FILESTREAM_TRANSACTION_CONTEXT
functions.doc: Returns a token for the current transaction that client applications use to bind FILESTREAM file system operations to it; NULL outside a transaction.

functions.name: MIN_ACTIVE_ROWVERSION
functions.doc: Returns the lowest rowversion value still active in the database, i.e. not yet committed; useful for change tracking with rowversion.

functions.name: DATALENGTH
functions.doc: Returns the number of bytes used to store a value, including trailing spaces. Returns bigint for max types and NULL for NULL input.

functions.name: CONNECTIONPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns a property of the current connection, such as transport protocol, auth scheme or client network address.

functions.name: GETANSINULL
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the database default allows NULL for new columns (ANSI null default), otherwise 0.

functions.name: TRIGGER_NESTLEVEL
functions.doc: Returns how many triggers fired the current statement, or how many times a given trigger fired, to detect trigger recursion.

functions.name: COLUMNS_UPDATED
functions.doc: Inside a DML trigger, returns a bit pattern showing which columns were inserted or updated.

functions.name: EVENTDATA
functions.doc: Inside a DDL or logon trigger, returns XML describing the server or database event that fired it.

functions.name: SESSIONPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns the current value of a SET option for the session, 1 if on and 0 if off.

functions.name: SQL_VARIANT_PROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns base type and other metadata about a sql_variant value.

functions.name: COLLATIONPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns a property of the given collation, such as its code page or locale ID.

functions.name: TERTIARY_WEIGHTS
functions.doc: Returns the tertiary sort weights for each character of a non-Unicode string under a SQL tertiary collation.

functions.name: GET_TRANSMISSION_STATUS
functions.doc: Returns the status of the last Service Broker transmission for one side of a conversation; empty string if successful.

functions.name: PUBLISHINGSERVERNAME
functions.doc: Returns the name of the original publishing server for a published database in database mirroring or availability groups.

functions.name: OBJECT_ID
functions.doc: Returns the object ID of a schema-scoped object, or NULL if not found. Accepts one- to three-part names; use tempdb..#name for temp tables.

functions.name: OBJECT_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the name of a schema-scoped object from its object ID, optionally in another database.

functions.name: OBJECT_SCHEMA_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the schema name of a schema-scoped object from its object ID.

functions.name: OBJECT_DEFINITION
functions.doc: Returns the T-SQL source of a module such as a view, procedure, function or trigger; NULL if encrypted or not permitted.

functions.name: OBJECTPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns information about a schema-scoped object in the current database, e.g. IsUserTable or IsProcedure.

functions.name: OBJECTPROPERTYEX
functions.doc: Returns information about a schema-scoped object, supporting more properties than OBJECTPROPERTY, such as BaseType.

functions.name: SCHEMA_ID
functions.doc: Returns the ID of the named schema, or of the caller's default schema when no name is given.

functions.name: SCHEMA_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the name of the schema with the given ID, or of the caller's default schema when no ID is given.

functions.name: DB_ID
functions.doc: Returns the ID of the named database, or of the current database when no name is given.

functions.name: DB_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the name of the database with the given ID, or of the current database when no ID is given.

functions.name: COL_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the column name for the given table ID and column ID.

functions.name: COL_LENGTH
functions.doc: Returns the defined length of a column in bytes; -1 for max types. Often used to test whether a column exists.

functions.name: COLUMNPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns information about a column or procedure parameter, such as AllowsNull, IsIdentity or Precision.

functions.name: TYPE_ID
functions.doc: Returns the ID of a data type by name; qualify user-defined types with their schema.

functions.name: TYPE_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the unqualified name of a data type from its type ID.

functions.name: TYPEPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns information about a data type, such as its precision or whether it allows NULL.

functions.name: DATABASEPROPERTYEX
functions.doc: Returns the current setting of a database option or property, e.g. Status, Recovery, Collation or Updateability.

functions.name: SERVERPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns information about the server instance, e.g. ProductVersion, Edition, MachineName, InstanceName or Collation.

functions.name: INDEX_COL
functions.doc: Returns the name of the key column at the given position in an index.

functions.name: INDEXPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns a property of a named index or statistics object, such as IsClustered, IsUnique or IndexDepth.

functions.name: INDEXKEY_PROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns information about a key column of an index, such as its column ID or sort direction.

functions.name: FILE_ID
functions.doc: Returns the file ID for a logical file name in the current database. Deprecated; use FILE_IDEX.

functions.name: FILE_IDEX
functions.doc: Returns the file ID for a logical data, log or full-text file name in the current database.

functions.name: FILE_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the logical file name for a file ID in the current database.

functions.name: FILEGROUP_ID
functions.doc: Returns the ID of the named filegroup.

functions.name: FILEGROUP_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the name of the filegroup with the given ID.

functions.name: FILEGROUPPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns the value of a property for the named filegroup.

functions.name: FILEPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns a property of a database file by logical name, e.g. SpaceUsed in 8-KB pages.

functions.name: APPLOCK_MODE
functions.doc: Returns the lock mode the owner holds on an application lock resource, or NoLock.

functions.name: APPLOCK_TEST
functions.doc: Returns 1 if an application lock could be granted with the given mode right now without blocking, otherwise 0.

functions.name: STATS_DATE
functions.doc: Returns when the statistics object on a table or indexed view was last updated.

functions.name: ASSEMBLYPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns information about a property of a registered CLR assembly.

functions.name: PARSENAME
functions.doc: Returns one part of a dot-separated name: 1 = object, 2 = schema, 3 = database, 4 = server. Does not check that the object exists.

functions.name: ORIGINAL_DB_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the database name specified in the connection string, or the login default database if none was given.

functions.name: FULLTEXTCATALOGPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns information about a full-text catalog property, such as ItemCount or PopulateStatus.

functions.name: FULLTEXTSERVICEPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns information about a property of the full-text engine, such as IsFullTextInstalled or LoadOSResources.

functions.name: USER_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the database user name for the given ID, or the current user when omitted.

functions.name: USER_ID
functions.doc: Returns the database principal ID for a user name. Deprecated; use DATABASE_PRINCIPAL_ID.

functions.name: DATABASE_PRINCIPAL_ID
functions.doc: Returns the ID of a database principal, or of the current user when no name is given.

functions.name: SUSER_NAME
functions.doc: Returns the login name for a server principal ID, or the current login when omitted.

functions.name: SUSER_SNAME
functions.doc: Returns the login name associated with a security identifier (SID), or the current login when omitted.

functions.name: SUSER_ID
functions.doc: Returns the server principal ID of a login, or of the current login when omitted.

functions.name: SUSER_SID
functions.doc: Returns the security identifier (SID) of a login, or of the current login when omitted.

functions.name: IS_MEMBER
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the current user is a member of the Windows group or database role, 0 if not, NULL if it is invalid.

functions.name: IS_SRVROLEMEMBER
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the login (default: current) is a member of the fixed or user-defined server role, 0 if not, NULL if invalid.

functions.name: IS_ROLEMEMBER
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the database principal (default: current user) is a member of the database role, 0 if not, NULL if invalid.

functions.name: HAS_PERMS_BY_NAME
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the current user has the given effective permission on a securable, 0 if not, NULL if the query is invalid.

functions.name: HAS_DBACCESS
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the current user can access the database, 0 if not, NULL if the name is invalid.

functions.name: PERMISSIONS
functions.doc: Returns a bitmap of the current user's statement, object or column permissions. Deprecated; use HAS_PERMS_BY_NAME or fn_my_permissions.

functions.name: ORIGINAL_LOGIN
functions.doc: Returns the login that first connected to the instance, even after impersonation with EXECUTE AS.

functions.name: CURRENT_USER
functions.doc: Returns the name of the current database user, reflecting EXECUTE AS context. Equivalent to USER_NAME(); written without parentheses.

functions.name: SESSION_USER
functions.doc: Returns the user name of the current context in the current database. Written without parentheses.

functions.name: SYSTEM_USER
functions.doc: Returns the login name of the current context, like SUSER_SNAME(). Written without parentheses.

functions.name: USER
functions.doc: Returns the database user name of the current context, equivalent to USER_NAME(). Written without parentheses.

functions.name: LOGINPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns information about the password policy settings of a SQL Server login.

functions.name: PWDCOMPARE
functions.doc: Hashes a clear-text password and returns 1 if it matches the given password hash, otherwise 0. Useful for finding weak passwords.

functions.name: PWDENCRYPT
functions.doc: Returns the SQL Server password hash of the input using the current hashing algorithm.

functions.name: ENCRYPTBYKEY
functions.doc: Encrypts data with a symmetric key identified by its GUID (see KEY_GUID). The key must be opened first with OPEN SYMMETRIC KEY.

functions.name: DECRYPTBYKEY
functions.doc: Decrypts data encrypted with a symmetric key; the key must already be open in the session. Returns NULL if no suitable key is open.

functions.name: ENCRYPTBYPASSPHRASE
functions.doc: Encrypts data with a symmetric key derived from a passphrase.

functions.name: DECRYPTBYPASSPHRASE
functions.doc: Decrypts data encrypted with ENCRYPTBYPASSPHRASE using the same passphrase; returns NULL if it does not match.

functions.name: ENCRYPTBYCERT
functions.doc: Encrypts data with the public key of a certificate.

functions.name: DECRYPTBYCERT
functions.doc: Decrypts data with the private key of a certificate.

functions.name: ENCRYPTBYASYMKEY
functions.doc: Encrypts data with an asymmetric key.

functions.name: DECRYPTBYASYMKEY
functions.doc: Decrypts data with the private key of an asymmetric key.

functions.name: DECRYPTBYKEYAUTOCERT
functions.doc: Decrypts data with a symmetric key that is automatically opened using a certificate.

functions.name: DECRYPTBYKEYAUTOASYMKEY
functions.doc: Decrypts data with a symmetric key that is automatically opened using an asymmetric key.

functions.name: CERT_ID
functions.doc: Returns the ID of a certificate in the current database.

functions.name: KEY_ID
functions.doc: Returns the ID of a symmetric key in the current database; prefix with # for a temporary key.

functions.name: KEY_GUID
functions.doc: Returns the GUID of a symmetric key in the current database, as needed by ENCRYPTBYKEY.

functions.name: ASYMKEY_ID
functions.doc: Returns the ID of an asymmetric key in the current database.

functions.name: CERTPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns the value of a certificate property, such as its expiry date or subject.

functions.name: ASYMKEYPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns a property of an asymmetric key, such as its algorithm.

functions.name: SYMKEYPROPERTY
functions.doc: Returns the algorithm of a symmetric key created from an EKM module.

functions.name: SIGNBYCERT
functions.doc: Signs text with a certificate and returns the signature.

functions.name: SIGNBYASYMKEY
functions.doc: Signs plaintext with an asymmetric key and returns the signature.

functions.name: VERIFYSIGNEDBYCERT
functions.doc: Returns 1 if data and signature match the given certificate, otherwise 0.

functions.name: VERIFYSIGNEDBYASYMKEY
functions.doc: Returns 1 if data and signature match the given asymmetric key, otherwise 0.

functions.name: IS_OBJECTSIGNED
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the object is signed by the certificate or asymmetric key with the given thumbprint, otherwise 0.

functions.name: CRYPT_GEN_RANDOM
functions.doc: Returns a cryptographically random binary value of the given length (1-8000 bytes) from the CryptoAPI.

functions.name: CERTENCODED
functions.doc: Returns the public portion of a certificate in binary DER form, usable with CREATE CERTIFICATE ... FROM BINARY.

functions.name: CERTPRIVATEKEY
functions.doc: Returns the private key of a certificate in binary form, encrypted with encryption_password.

functions.name: CURSOR_STATUS
functions.doc: Reports whether a cursor or cursor variable is open with rows (1), open but empty (0), closed (-1), not allocated (-2) or does not exist (-3).

functions.name: OPENROWSET

signatures.doc: Ad hoc access to remote data through an OLE DB provider.
Reads a file as a rowset or as a single LOB value.

functions.doc: Reads remote data via an OLE DB provider, or a file via BULK, as a table usable in FROM. Ad hoc provider access requires the Ad Hoc Distributed Queries option.

functions.name: OPENQUERY
functions.doc: Runs a pass-through query on a linked server and exposes the result as a table in FROM. The query must be a literal string up to 8 KB.

functions.name: OPENDATASOURCE
functions.doc: Supplies ad hoc connection information as the server part of a four-part object name, without defining a linked server.

functions.name: OPENXML
functions.doc: Shreds an XML document prepared with sp_xml_preparedocument into rows. Add WITH (schema_declaration | table_name) to shape the columns.

functions.name: STRING_SPLIT

signatures.doc: SQL Server 2022+: 1 adds an ordinal column with 1-based positions.

functions.doc: Splits a string into rows (column value) on a single-character separator. Output order is not guaranteed without enable_ordinal. Needs compatibility level 130.

functions.name: GENERATE_SERIES
functions.doc: Returns a one-column table (value) of numbers from start to stop, stepping by step (default 1 or -1). Requires compatibility level 160.

functions.name: CONTAINSTABLE
functions.doc: Full-text search returning a table of KEY and RANK columns for rows matching a CONTAINS-style condition.

functions.name: FREETEXTTABLE
functions.doc: Full-text search returning a table of KEY and RANK columns for rows whose meaning matches the free-text string.

functions.name: SEMANTICKEYPHRASETABLE
functions.doc: Returns statistically significant key phrases found in columns with semantic indexing.

functions.name: SEMANTICSIMILARITYTABLE
functions.doc: Returns documents that are semantically similar to a given document in columns with semantic indexing.

functions.name: SEMANTICSIMILARITYDETAILSTABLE
functions.doc: Returns the key phrases that two semantically indexed documents have in common.

functions.name: PREDICT
functions.doc: Scores data with a stored machine learning model and returns predictions; declare output columns with a WITH clause.

functions.name: CONTAINS
functions.doc: Full-text predicate used in WHERE; matches words, phrases, prefixes, proximity or inflections in full-text indexed columns.

functions.name: FREETEXT
functions.doc: Full-text predicate used in WHERE; matches rows by the meaning of the search text rather than its exact wording.

functions.name: TEXTPTR
functions.doc: Returns the text pointer of a text, ntext or image column for use with READTEXT, WRITETEXT and UPDATETEXT.

functions.name: TEXTVALID
functions.doc: Returns 1 if a text, ntext or image pointer is valid, otherwise 0.

functions.name: XML_SCHEMA_NAMESPACE
functions.doc: Rebuilds and returns the XML schemas stored in an XML schema collection, optionally only for one target namespace.

functions.name: @@CONNECTIONS
functions.doc: Number of attempted connections, successful or not, since SQL Server last started.

functions.name: @@CPU_BUSY
functions.doc: Ticks of CPU time SQL Server has spent working since it last started; multiply by @@TIMETICKS for microseconds.

functions.name: @@CURSOR_ROWS
functions.doc: Qualifying row count of the last cursor opened on the connection: -m while populating asynchronously, -1 for dynamic cursors, 0 if none open.

functions.name: @@DATEFIRST
functions.doc: Current SET DATEFIRST value for the session, i.e. the first day of the week (1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday; U.S. English default is 7).

functions.name: @@DBTS
functions.doc: Last-used rowversion (timestamp) value of the current database.

functions.name: @@ERROR
functions.doc: Error number of the last executed statement, or 0 if it succeeded. Reset by each statement, so capture it immediately.

functions.name: @@FETCH_STATUS
functions.doc: Result of the last FETCH on the connection: 0 = success, -1 = failed or past the result set, -2 = row missing, -9 = no fetch.

functions.name: @@IDENTITY
functions.doc: Last identity value inserted in the session in any scope, including by triggers. SCOPE_IDENTITY() is usually safer.

functions.name: @@IDLE
functions.doc: Ticks SQL Server has been idle since it last started; multiply by @@TIMETICKS for microseconds.

functions.name: @@IO_BUSY
functions.doc: Ticks SQL Server has spent on input and output operations since it last started.

functions.name: @@LANGID
functions.doc: Local language ID of the language currently in use by the session.

functions.name: @@LANGUAGE
functions.doc: Name of the language currently in use by the session.

functions.name: @@LOCK_TIMEOUT
functions.doc: Current lock timeout of the session in milliseconds; -1 means wait indefinitely (the default).

functions.name: @@MAX_CONNECTIONS
functions.doc: Maximum number of simultaneous user connections the instance allows, not necessarily the configured value.

functions.name: @@MAX_PRECISION
functions.doc: Precision used by the decimal and numeric types on the server, 38 by default.

functions.name: @@NESTLEVEL
functions.doc: Nesting level of the current module execution: 0 at the top level, incremented by each nested call (maximum 32).

functions.name: @@OPTIONS
functions.doc: Bit mask describing the SET options currently enabled for the session.

functions.name: @@PACK_RECEIVED
functions.doc: Number of input network packets read by SQL Server since it last started.

functions.name: @@PACK_SENT
functions.doc: Number of output network packets written by SQL Server since it last started.

functions.name: @@PACKET_ERRORS
functions.doc: Number of network packet errors on SQL Server connections since it last started.

functions.name: @@PROCID
functions.doc: Object ID of the currently executing module, such as a stored procedure, trigger or user-defined function.

functions.name: @@REMSERVER
functions.doc: Name of the remote server as it appears in the login record. Deprecated.

functions.name: @@ROWCOUNT
functions.doc: Number of rows affected or read by the last statement. Use ROWCOUNT_BIG() when the count can exceed 2 billion.

functions.name: @@SERVERNAME
functions.doc: Name of the local server running SQL Server, including the instance name for named instances.

functions.name: @@SERVICENAME
functions.doc: Registry key name of the SQL Server service: MSSQLSERVER for a default instance, otherwise the instance name.

functions.name: @@SPID
functions.doc: Session ID of the current user process.

functions.name: @@TEXTSIZE
functions.doc: Current SET TEXTSIZE value: maximum bytes of large-value or text/ntext/image data returned by a SELECT.

functions.name: @@TIMETICKS
functions.doc: Number of microseconds per tick, used to convert @@CPU_BUSY, @@IDLE and @@IO_BUSY.

functions.name: @@TOTAL_ERRORS
functions.doc: Number of disk write errors encountered by SQL Server since it last started.

functions.name: @@TOTAL_READ
functions.doc: Number of physical disk reads performed by SQL Server since it last started.

functions.name: @@TOTAL_WRITE
functions.doc: Number of physical disk writes performed by SQL Server since it last started.

functions.name: @@TRANCOUNT
functions.doc: Number of BEGIN TRANSACTION statements currently open on the connection; 0 means no active transaction.

functions.name: @@VERSION
functions.doc: Version, edition, build, processor architecture and operating system details of the current SQL Server installation.
